    Block equations of maps between push-downs #

    Proof of Proposition 4.7, first paragraph. For a quiver morphism p : D → Q and representations X, Y of D, a linear map f : ⊕ X(i) → ⊕ Y(i) commutes with the push-down actions (IsPdHom) if and only if its blocks bl f j i = e_j f e_i satisfy the equations (BlockEqs): blocks between different fibres vanish, and for each arrow c of Q, ∑_β f_{j,t(β)} X(β) = ∑_α Y(α) f_{s(α),i} over the arrows β labelled c leaving i and α labelled c entering j.

    When p is injective on arrows with a fixed source and on those with a fixed target, each equation involves only blocks at the two ends of one edge of the matching quiver. Hence retaining the blocks on a set of positions closed under these edges (Saturated) preserves the equations (blockEqs_restr), and the diagonal blocks of a map satisfying the equations form a morphism of representations (diagHom).
